transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-27
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Janelle Rivera (Redwood AE), Noah Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Marigold VP Product), Ethan Ward (Eng Lead), Sofia Jimenez (Security), Liam Brooks (Data Scientist)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough): Quick discovery focused on Marigold's PLG path. They want fastest time-to-first-token for a product demo next month, evaluate hosted vs dedicated vs private options for compliance and latency/cost tradeoffs. Action: Redwood to share credits, docs, and SOC2/KMS materials; Marigold to run smoke tests.

Topics: quickstart credits, time-to-first-token (TTFT), demo latency, dedicated/reserved capacity, private/VPC and KMS, RBAC/SSO, data residency, evaluation plan.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Janelle: hey everyone, thanks for carving time, i'm janelle with Redwood Inference, i'll hand over to noah in a sec but main goal is to understand where marigold is on the self-serve path and what's the minimal path to a working demo.
[00:12] Priya: thanks, yeah, appreciate it. ours is pretty simple we need to ship a demo for a partner meeting mid-april, so ideally time-to-first-token, like how fast can we get a call from our app into a model and get a response. budget is limited so we want to evaluate the free credits/quickstart first.
[00:28] Noah: great, that is achievable. quick note — when you say demo do you mean low-latency interactive or batch generation?
[00:34] Priya: interactive, sub-second or low-single-second ideally for single-turn product descriptions. it's not huge scale, maybe 500–1k calls per day during the demo window.
[00:43] Ethan: and just to add, our infra is on GCP us-west2, we currently call OpenAI for some prototypes but looking for better cost predictability and improved latency to our region.
[00:55] Janelle: cool — so two axes: ttft (time to first token) and production fit (latency/cost/SLA). for ttft, our self-serve flow gets you from signup to a token in under an hour typically, often under 15 minutes if you're just doing a quick cURL. we'll share a quickstart script and seed prompts with credits.
[01:15] Priya: under an hour, nice. what about data — we handle partner PII and the legal team will ask about retention and encryption, SOC2, things like that.
[01:25] Noah: yes, we are SOC 2 certified, and for hosted customers we offer at-rest encryption and customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM for private deployments, and we can show the audit docs. note: in hosted mode default we still retain logs for 30 days for debugging unless you opt-out via the data retention settings.
[01:44] Sofia: clarification, when you say KMS for private, is that a managed key integration or do you bring your own HSM? we have strict control requirements.
[01:52] Noah: for our Private (we sometimes say Redbud Private in internal notes, sorry) you can integrate your KMS, bring your own HSM via an appliance or cloud KMS, and we provide the key wrap hooks. for Dedicated we support customer-managed keys in cloud provider KMS too. we'll send the KMS integration playbook.
[02:10] Liam: a couple of perf questions — does the hosted model catalog include quantized variants? we care about cost per token and may want a 4-bit-ish model for cheaper inference.
[02:18] Janelle: yep, catalog includes curated open models and we surface quantized variants where supported. Redwood Optimize gives suggestions on quantization and batching to reduce cost. but small note, quantization can impact output quality so you'll want eval sets.
[02:35] Ethan: ok on evals. for our demo we have 3 prompt templates and ~500 tokens average per call. what'd you recommend for batching? we need low latency so maybe no big batching but maybe prefix cache?
[02:47] Noah: for interactive low-latency we avoid big batching; instead we rely on prefix/KV caching. that's our continuous caching for repeated prompts. it preserves latency while reducing token compute for repeated prefixes. sometimes the transcript will say K V cash or K V cache in our notes, so beware auto-transcribe.
[03:05] Priya: and what about dedicated? is that overkill for a demo? what's the minimum commit?
[03:11] Janelle: dedicated is typically for predictable sustained throughput. we have small reserved tiers for early enterprise customers but for a demo with 1k calls/day hosted with credits should be fine. Dedicated monthly commits usually start at X units — i'll put exact tiers in the follow-up doc; for now assume dedicated is higher cost but gives more predictability and isolation.
[03:34] Ethan: any latency numbers to share for hosted from us-west2 to your hosted infra? we tried another provider and saw 500–700ms median which was rough.
[03:43] Noah: depending on model size and region, our hosted median single-turn can be 200–450ms for mid-size models (e.g., 7B quantized), 700–1200ms for larger models. we'll attach per-model perf profiles. note that real numbers depend on sequence length and KV cache hitrate.
[04:02] Sofia: security question — do you support SSO/SAML and role-based access control?"
[04:07] Janelle: yes, we support SSO SAML for enterprise console and RBAC for tokens and route-level permissions. plus audit logs. for hosted trials you can start with simple API keys and then we can enable SSO on Dedicated/Private.
[04:22] Priya: timeline wise, if we want to push a demo in mid-april, is there any risk in running the quickstart now and then switching to dedicated later? data migration or model pinning concerns?
[04:33] Noah: switching is straightforward — you pin model versions and rollout policies. your prompts and evals are portable. one caveat: dedicated/reserved clusters might use slightly different model variants optimized for throughput; we have compatibility matrix and migration notes. we'll highlight auto-fallback policies too so you have graceful degradation if dedicated capacity is constrained.
[04:56] Ethan: do you have a sample cURL or minimal app?
[04:59] Janelle: yes, quickstart repo link will be in the follow-up. typical path: signup -> get credits -> create API key -> run sample request (curl or node snippet) -> get response. usually people hit first response in under 10 minutes once they set env vars.
[05:14] Liam: noise in transcription here, but how do you handle observability — we want per-route latency/cost visibility and tracing into per-token cost.
[05:24] Noah: Redwood Console exposes token-level cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and traces. there's also a rollout UI for canary and A/B tests and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. we'll give you a sandbox link for the console.
[05:38] Priya: budget question — if we go beyond credits and into low-volume production, is there a small plan or pay-as-you-go?
[05:45] Janelle: yes hosted is usage-based (per-token) and we have small monthly tiers for startups. Dedicated is committed monthly. we'll include a rough cost calculator in the follow-up.
[05:58] Ethan: about compliance: we will need SOC2 Type II report and some pen-test summary to share with legal. also data residency — some partners require EU only.
[06:09] Noah: SOC2 Type II is available; pen test summary available on request. for data residency we have hosted regions in NA and EU; Private deployments allow on-prem air-gapped if you need that. Dedicated can be placed in specific cloud regions. we'll attach the compliance pack.
[06:31] Sofia: on private/on-prem — what is the lift for us? we run mostly GCP but have on-prem infra for sensitive workloads.
[06:39] Noah: private comes in two flavors: VPC-hosted private with customer-managed networking (lower lift) or full on-prem package (higher lift, air-gapped). typical POC is 2–6 weeks for VPC setup, longer for on-prem. we'll map steps in the doc.
[06:56] Priya: ok good. what's the low-friction evaluation you recommend now?
[07:00] Janelle: start with hosted PLG: accept credits, run quickstart, do your smoke test with the 3 prompts, send us perf numbers. if you see model quality variance, we can suggest quantization vs bigger model tradeoffs.
[07:13] Ethan: what are realistic perf expectations for our 500 token average per call?
[07:18] Noah: for 500 tokens on a 7B quantized model you might hit ~300–700ms depending on cache hitrate and prefix reuse. for larger models expect 900ms+. we'll provide per-model graphs.
[07:31] Priya: will you help set up the tokens and credits or is that self-serve?
[07:35] Janelle: we'll provision starter credits and a sandbox org and send instructions; it's self-serve but we'll be hands-on for the first hour if you want pairing.
[07:44] Liam: any gotchas with rate limits?
[07:47] Noah: hosted has default rate limits to protect noisy tenants; we can temporarily raise limits for your pilot if you need it. Dedicated eliminates noisy neighbor issues.
[07:59] Priya: great. anything we should pre-share to make the smoke test easier?
[08:03] Janelle: share sample prompts, expected token counts, and region. also your current stack call pattern (sync/async) and auth flow.
[08:13] Ethan: we'll share the sample app and request a sandbox org.
[08:16] Janelle: perfect. i'll follow up with the quickstart link, credits, perf profiles, SOC2 + KMS playbook, and a short cost calculator.
[08:27] Priya: awesome. last quick question — do you have any auto-billing or invoice for small pilots? we prefer a PO for accounting.
[08:34] Janelle: yes we can do invoices for pilots; our finance folks will coordinate. for PLG it's card and then we can convert to invoice for committed pilots.
[08:43] Sofia: okay can we get a follow up focused on security and KMS integration?
[08:47] Noah: yes we'll schedule a 30-minute technical security deep dive with our security SE and include a KMS walkthrough.
[08:54] Janelle: thanks everyone — quick recap in one sentence?
[08:58] Priya: quickstart hosted trial with credits, run smoke tests, evaluate latency, then decide on Dedicated/Private for demo if needed.
[09:06] Janelle: perfect. i'll send the onboarding packet today and we'll target pilot kickoff week of 4/6 once you confirm smoke test.
[09:14] Ethan: thanks all, appreciate the clarity.
[09:16] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-ops: Redwood Private sometimes transcribed as Redbud/private; K V cache -> K V cash; some names like Priya occasionally become Preeya in auto-text.
notes: Follow-up must attach quickstart link, SOC2 pack, KMS integration doc, perf profiles, and sandbox org details.
